description.narrative: Wefaq conducted a needs assessment in May 2021, after the escalation in Gaza, which showed that women in Rafah needed additional psychological support as well as in-depth multi-sectoral interventions. Based on the results of this needs assessment the response wasdesigned. The proposed project aims to increase the access of vulnerable women in Rafah governorate to safe, structured and coordinated multi-sectoral services. The designed interventions include providing psychological support to women survivors of GBV through the provision of at least 6-8 collective sessions, followed by individual sessions for each survivor. This intervention, which is based on the severity of the cases, is centred on the manual that was credited from GBV SC members, prepared in a participatory approach. Wefaq has a hotline alongside remote modalities, such as Zoom, WebEx or WhatsApp applications, according to the beneficiaries’ choice of communication, which ensures their privacy and safety, including the option for in person at Wefaq HQ if preferred. Other interventions include: the provision of legal consultations to 30 women and girls, and court representation to 30 women and married girls, especially survivors of GBV; the distribution of 150 dignity kits (in line withGBV SC standards and based on vulnerability selection criteria); organizing a community meeting with stakeholders; making videos to inaugurate the project and sharing it on CBOs websites and social media. Referral of (20) traumatized women and girls, including women with disabilities to a psychiatrist and coordination with MHPSS department in the Ministry of Health for severe cases; case management services to 45 women; and providing foodvouchers to 150HHs of targeted women. after coordination with CWG.

participating-org.narrative: Wefaq Association for Women and Child Care is an independent, non-profit Palestinian women’s association established in 2010, aiming to achieve gender equality through economic empowerment and psychological support programs to support marginalized groupsin the southern Gaza Strip, especially in the governorates of Rafah and Khan Yunis. From 1996 until 2009 under the name of the Women’s Department, where it was working under the umbrella of the Gaza Mental Health Program, and due to the change in policiesand the expansion of the program’s field of work into a knowledge-based organization focusing on practical research, training and advocacy, a restructuring process for the program took place which This resulted in the development of the Women's Departmentinto an independent association under the name Wefaq Association for the Care of Women and Children with license number (8155).
